.NET · Automation / Development note

Retry without duplicates. Approve without skipping steps.

A runnable example with an HTTP contract, idempotency and version checks. Connecting API logic with an approval workflow.

By Sergio Hernández7 November 2026
In this note
  1. Two identifiers with different responsibilities
  2. Approval is an explicit transition
  3. Reproduce the contract before adding a connector
  4. Add Power Automate with a recovery path

When automation receives no response, it can repeat a request the server already processed. The request prototype separates that replay from the approval decision and subsequent state changes.

Two identifiers with different responsibilities

requestId identifies the business request. Idempotency-Key identifies the logical creation attempt. The same key and data return the existing record; the same key with different data returns 409. A different key with the same requestId is also rejected.

The prototype trims field values and uppercases the identifier before comparison. Keys remain in memory until the process restarts. It provides no cross-server or post-restart deduplication and no exactly-once execution guarantee.

Approval is an explicit transition

The valid journey is received, in review, approved and completed. Review can also end in rejection. The API requires the expected version and returns 409 if another change happened first.

A version counter prevents overwriting newer state, but does not identify the approver. The example runs locally without authentication. In a real deployment, identity, permissions and durable records belong to the server.

Reproduce the contract before adding a connector

The browser demo and .NET domain run the same JSON scenarios: creation, replay, changed-data conflict, rejection, invalid transition and old version. HTTP checks start the local API and verify the actual exchange.

The API limits body size, rejects unknown fields and returns Problem Details errors. Stable codes distinguish invalid input from conflicts. Repeating an invalid request does not fix validation.

Add Power Automate with a recovery path

The repository guide proposes registering a request, starting review and waiting for an authorised person’s decision. The flow keeps requestId and key across retries rather than creating a new key for every failed call.

After an uncertain response, read the current state before proceeding. Separate errors into scopes with Run After and log context without secrets. The guide is not deployed in a tenant and assumes no free connectors: permissions, connectivity and licences depend on the environment.

Putting it into practice

Make retries, decisions and conflicts part of the contract. Test those paths before connecting them to a real process.
